source_supported_links: introduced Apis mellifera is the most common visitor
original pollinators inferred as long-proboscis moths from floral traits and scent
Apis pollen transfer is unidirectional from short-styled to long-styled morph
the stated mechanism is inability of Apis to reach hidden stigmas of short-styled flowers
long-styled flowers have 1.7-38 times the field fruit set of short-styled flowers
hand and open pollination plus pollen-tube growth were examined

sources.source_table_note: The review table explicitly cites both prior published work and K. Watanabe/T. Sugawara unpublished data for P. homalosperma. Values are admissible as published table-level evidence, not as recovered individual raw rows.

source_supported_links: P. homalosperma is morphologically and functionally distylous
stigma and anther heights are not exactly reciprocal
long-styled flowers are completely self- and intramorph-incompatible
short-styled morph is more abundant in three examined island populations

source_native_construct.upstream_change: anthropogenically disrupted pollinator fauna with inferred replacement of long-proboscis moth function by introduced short-tongued honeybees
source_native_construct.plant_state_axis: distylous stigma position: exposed long-styled stigma versus hidden short-styled stigma
source_native_construct.effectiveness_link: Apis cannot reach the hidden short-styled stigma and pollen transfer is reported only from S morph to L morph
source_native_construct.reproductive_link: field fruit set is strongly higher in L morph despite nearly symmetric high intermorph hand-pollination fruit set in the published table
source_native_construct.why_not_signed_numeric: No source-native honeybee proboscis-length minus stigma-depth or analogous numeric mismatch value has been recovered. Corolla tube length or honeybee tongue length from secondary literature must not be substituted as the primary signed position.

propagation_classification.reason: The current dominant visitor is physically unable to service one stigma position, pollen flow becomes directional, and the recipient-accessible L morph has much higher field fruit set. High and nearly symmetric intermorph hand-pollination fruit set argues that the field asymmetry is not simply a directional intrinsic compatibility failure.
propagation_classification.relation_to_hawaii_buffering: Ogasawara provides a contrasting case where access/effectiveness mismatch is associated with a strong reproductive asymmetry, whereas Hawaii 2026 shows interaction-quality change buffered before reproductive collapse.
propagation_classification.relation_to_v12: Supports functional state/access as a branch-relevant variable but does not provide the source-native numeric signed position needed to validate the v12 signed-position law.

allowed_claim: In P. homalosperma, an introduced honeybee-dominated contemporary pollination system produces a source-described physical access asymmetry and unidirectional pollen transfer, while field fruit set differs strongly between floral morphs even though published intermorph hand-pollination fruit set is high in both directions.
blocked_claims: do not claim direct experimental causation by historical pollinator replacement
do not call the categorical access state a source-native numeric signed-position measurement
do not infer a honeybee proboscis length from family/guild or secondary values
do not call open fruit-set asymmetry a controlled all-pollinator dependency estimate
do not call the cross-study evidence a same-tagged-individual causal chain
do not infer that the observed process has already caused dioecy or another floral evolutionary transition
next_actions: Search only named lawful article/supplement/institutional sources for exact floral-position and honeybee access measurements if they become available.
Do not block comparative propagation synthesis on unavailable raw rows: the published quantitative hand/open fruit contrast is already admissible at table level.
Use this system as a propagation contrast against buffered Hawaii, not as proof of a universal access-to-reproduction coefficient.
claim_boundary: This audit strengthens a propagation example but remains a partial bridge. The replacement history is inferred, direct effectiveness is categorical rather than standardized per visit, and no numeric signed mismatch or controlled total dependency estimand is recovered.
